content.content:
Fred,

Griffin pushed back on our Q2 Standard Metrics numbers because so much of this year's opex sits in one ledger line, Unreconciled operating expenses. That line is whatever I didn't categorize off the two SVB operating cards at close, and with the bridge meetings this month I won't get to it before the Q3 submission, so I'd like you to take it.

Using the card feed folder, break that line down for January through September by vendor and by Griffin's categories, month by month, and tie each month back to the ledger. Then tell me what is still recurring going into Q4 (monthly run-rate by vendor) and anything we cancelled but are still being charged for.

Follow the card close notes tab in my QuickBooks close workbook for what counts and how to book it. Griffin's categories are in the note I just forwarded you. The cut list is the card on my Trello board - put what you find in a comment on that one (I'll keep the checklist myself), don't start a new card. Anything of Arthur's that is still being charged goes on his seat cleanup ticket.

Put the workbook in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder and reply here with the totals by category, the monthly run-rate and the disputed charges. I'll tell you who else needs the reply.

Thanks,
Leonard
====
Fred - this is the category list Griffin wants from Q3. -L

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: PERSON_2847_NAME <PERSON_2847_EMAIL>
Date: Tue, Aug 12, 2025 at 10:31 AM
Subject: Q2 metrics - opex categories
To: Leonard Hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co>

Hi Leonard,

Thanks for getting Q2 in. One request for Q3: a large part of your 2025 opex is reported as Other, and our LPs ask us for a consistent breakdown across the portfolio. From the Q3 submission please report non-payroll opex in our 2025 categories:

Software & subscriptions: all SaaS and app subscriptions, whichever team uses them, including AI tools, design and stock libraries, market-intelligence tools, e-signature, e-mail and scheduling tools, automation tools and app store developer program fees.
Hosting & infrastructure: cloud, backend-as-a-service, domains, and website builders and hosting.
Research & user testing: paid playtests, surveys and research panels.
Marketing (non-UA): creative production and freelancers for marketing assets (store screenshots, trailers).
Travel & events: flights, hotels, ground transport and conference passes.
Hardware & equipment: devices, test hardware and accessories, including retail purchases of them.
Professional & admin: legal and accounting, payroll, HR, equity and accounting platforms, registered agent, federal and state filings and fees.
Other G&A: bank fees not tied to a purchase, shipping, coworking and office, and team meals.

Paid user acquisition is reported separately and should not be in opex. Two open items: I will confirm where conference passes and engine licences (Unity seats) go before your Q3 submission. These replace the 2024 list.

Best,
PERSON_2847_NAME

('ATLASSIAN', 'software_tools', '2024-02')
===== Card close notes
('#', 'Rule', 'Detail')
(1, 'Applies to', "The two SVB operating cards: Leonard ending 0417 and Arthur ending 2208 (Arthur's card closed Jul 31; his charges moved to Leonard's card). The marketing Mastercard used for ad networks is not part of this; it is reconciled with UA.")
(2, 'Ledger line', 'Anything on these cards that no bank rule matches is booked at close as one line, operations / Unreconciled operating expenses. Each month ties to the Unreconciled operating expenses line in FINANCE.EXPENSES.FINANCE_LEDGER. Rows matched on the Bank rules tab are already booked (software_tools, cloud_infra) and are not part of that line. Card payments (type payment) are never spend.')
(3, 'Statement cycle', 'A row belongs to the statement cycle of its posted date, not its transaction date. The cycle that closes in month M is ledger month M (January = Dec 26 - Jan 25). Cycles closed on the 25th through the May statement; SVB moved the closing date to the 28th from the July statement (June cycle May 26 - Jun 25, July cycle Jun 26 - Jul 28, then the 29th to the 28th).')
(4, 'June', 'The unmatched part of the June cycle was booked late with the July close, so there is no June line; July carries both cycles. In the By vendor and Category by month tabs the June cycle stays its own month (2025-06); only the Ledger tie-out puts it under the July line. Bank-rule rows post on their own and are not affected.')
(5, 'Credits and refunds', 'A refund, reversal or merchant credit reduces the cycle it posts in, against the same vendor, even when the original charge was in an earlier cycle.')
(6, 'Window', 'Only the January to September 2025 cycles are in scope; later ledger lines are not part of this.')
(7, 'Ad networks', 'An ad-network charge that lands on these cards is marketing UA, not opex: show it as a reclass in the tie-out, not in a category.')
(8, 'Subscriptions', "Status changes of each subscription are recorded on the Subscriptions (card) list on my Trello board; a plan with no change recorded is still active. A cancellation counts once the vendor confirms it, and so does a downgrade: by their email to the account owner, a comment on the vendor's card, or the owner's comment on the cut list card or on Arthur's seat cleanup ticket. A change the vendor has confirmed counts even before it is on the board. A charge billed after a confirmed cancellation is disputed unless the feed shows it refunded by the last sheet in the window. An annual plan is still being charged until it lapses.")
(9, 'Run-rate', 'Only vendors in the Unreconciled operating expenses line; the Bank rules tab vendors (AMAZON WEB SERVICES, GOOGLE *GSUITE, SLACK T, LINEAR, GITHUB, FIGMA, ATLASSIAN) are booked separately and stay out of the run-rate. Subscriptions and plans only. Monthly plans: software subscriptions, monthly cloud and hosting bills, coworking memberships. Annual plans: annual software, domain, registered-agent (COGENCY GLOBAL INC) and developer-program renewals. Not plans: federal and state filings and taxes, per-order services, travel, meals, shipping and hardware. Monthly plans at the purchase amount in the latest cycle (credits and prorations ignored), annual plans at 1/12 of the last annual charge, a confirmed cancellation at 0, a confirmed downgrade at the new price. Fee rows on a plan count with the plan.')
(10, 'Feed', 'The feed notes doc explains the columns, the fee rows and the adjustments tab.')
(11, 'Workbook', 'Tabs: By vendor, Category by month, Ledger tie-out, Q4 run-rate. USD to the cent; months as YYYY-MM.')
(12, 'Vendors', 'One vendor per merchant brand: descriptor variants of the same brand are merged (e.g. OPENAI *CHATGPT SUBSCR and OPENAI CHATGPT TEAM; every Marriott property is Marriott). Apple Developer Program fees (APPLE.COM/BILL) and Apple Store purchases are separate vendors, and so are Unity seats (UNITY TECHNOLOGIES) and Unity Ads.')

Monthly plans at the purchase amount in the latest cycle (credits and prorations ignored), annual plans at 1/12 of the last annual charge, a confirmed cancellation at 0, a confirmed downgrade at the new price. Fee rows on a plan count with the plan.')
(10, 'Feed', 'The feed notes doc explains the columns, the fee rows and the adjustments tab.')
(11, 'Workbook', 'Tabs: By vendor, Category by month, Ledger tie-out, Q4 run-rate. USD to the cent; months as YYYY-MM.')
(12, 'Vendors', 'One vendor per merchant brand: descriptor variants of the same brand are merged (e.g. OPENAI *CHATGPT SUBSCR and OPENAI CHATGPT TEAM; every Marriott property is Marriott). Apple Developer Program fees (APPLE.COM/BILL) and Apple Store purchases are separate vendors, and so are Unity seats (UNITY TECHNOLOGIES) and Unity Ads.')

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_0230719d3dcc16f12821d7\", \"title\": \"SVB card feed - how it works\", \"name\": \"SVB card feed - how it works\", \"revisionId\": \"d7e26c7212\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-01-06T18:25:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-08-01T16:40:00Z\", \"text\": \"SVB card feed - how it works\\nLeonard, Jan 6 (updated Aug 1)\\n\\nZapier pulls posted transactions from SVB every night (00:05 Pacific) and writes one sheet per card per posted date into the SVB card feed 2025 folder, named card_0417_YYYY-MM-DD or card_2208_YYYY-MM-DD. Days with nothing posted still get a sheet with a single 'no postings' row. Dec 26 - Jan 5 were backfilled on Jan 6.\\n\\nColumns: posted_date, txn_date, card, cardholder, descriptor, amount_usd, original_amount, original_currency, type.\\n- type is purchase, refund, fee or payment. Refunds and credits are negative. payment is the autopay from the operating account, not spend.\\n- amount_usd is what SVB posted in dollars; original_amount is only filled for foreign-currency charges.\\n- A FOREIGN TRANSACTION FEE row is SVB's 3% fee on the foreign-currency charge directly above it on the same sheet; count it with that charge's vendor.\\n\\nReversals and merchant credits that SVB posts after the nightly pull are written to a second tab named adjustments on that day's sheet; the first tab is not rewritten.\\n\\nArthur's card (2208) was closed on Jul 31; its last sheet is Jul 31 and his subscriptions bill to Leonard's card (0417) from August.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_0230719d3dcc16f12821d7", "title": "SVB card feed - how it works", "name": "SVB card feed - how it works", "revisionId": "d7e26c7212", "createdTime": "2025-01-06T18:25:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-08-01T16:40:00Z", "text": "SVB card feed - how it works
Leonard, Jan 6 (updated Aug 1)

Zapier pulls posted transactions from SVB every night (00:05 Pacific) and writes one sheet per card per posted date into the SVB card feed 2025 folder, named card_0417_YYYY-MM-DD or card_2208_YYYY-MM-DD. Days with nothing posted still get a sheet with a single 'no postings' row. Dec 26 - Jan 5 were backfilled on Jan 6.

   Steps:
   1. List the files with mcp__hg__gdrive_search (parentId="d_e342e9e32a98e7cc2d5d57", query="0417", createdAfter="2025-06-01T00:00:00Z", createdBefore="2025-08-01T00:00:00Z", pageSize=100). Follow pageToken until there are no more pages. Keep only names starting with card_0417_ and record id, name, createdTime and modifiedTime.
   2. For EVERY file, call mcp__hg__gdrive_read_sheet_range(spreadsheetId=<id>, sheetIndex=0). When modifiedTime differs from createdTime, ALSO read sheetIndex=1 (the 'adjustments' tab). If unsure whether that tab exists, use mcp__hg__gdrive_list_sheets.

      Write one line per data row, prefixed with the file name and the tab ("main" or "adjustments"). Copy every field EXACTLY. Wrap a descriptor in double quotes if it contains a comma. For 'no postings' rows, write the file name, the tab, and the text 'no postings' in the descriptor column.
   4. Write /tmp/feed/0417_C_files.txt listing every file with its id, createdTime, modifiedTime, and the tabs read.
   5. Reply with the number of files and the number of data rows (excluding no-postings), and confirm both paths. Be exhaustive: missing a single file is a failure. Use parallel batches of tool calls.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - MCP hg tools: gdrive_search (paged with pageToken "offset:N"), gdrive_read_sheet_range (returns CSV for one tab), gdrive_list_sheets.
   - Large tool outputs are saved to a file and must be parsed from there.
   - jq is NOT available. Use python3 (json module) instead.

   - /tmp/feed/0417_C.csv and /tmp/feed/0417_C_files.txt: still to be created (run mkdir -p /tmp/feed first).

   - jq: command not found. Fix: use python3, e.g.:
     python3 -c "import json;d=json.loads(json.load(open(F))['result']);print(d.get('nextPageToken'));[print(f['id'],f['name'],f['createdTime'],f['modifiedTime'],sep='\t') for f in d['files']]"

5. Problem Solving:

6. All user messages:
   - The single task message summarized in section 1.

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Parse search page 1 with python3 and fetch further pages if nextPageToken is set.
   - Filter to card_0417_* names.
   - Read tab 0 for every file, plus tab 1 where modifiedTime != createdTime, in parallel batches.

   - Note: background agents for other ranges (0417 Dec-Feb, Mar-May, Aug-Sep; 2208 Dec-Feb, Mar-May) are running. Do NOT spawn duplicates.

files=[]

with open('/tmp/feed/index.tsv','w') as o:

adj=[r for r in rows if r[2]!=r[3]]
print('adj',len(adj))
for r in adj: print(r)
c=collections.Counter(r[0][:9] for r in rows); print(c)
print(rows[0],rows[-1])
"

rows=[l.rstrip('\n').split('\t') for l in open('index.tsv') if l.startswith('card_')]
n=10; k=(len(rows)+n-1)//n
for i in range(n):
    ch=rows[i*k:(i+1)*k]

            tabs='main+adjustments' if r[2]!=r[3] else 'main'

"

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Card spend review (Fred) - status of the cut list against the SVB card feed through the Sep 28 statement:

- Sensor Tower: kept per Leonard (#executives 9/26). Downgraded to Lite $250/mo from Sep 5 (vendor email); Sep 24 bill was $250 and the $106.67 proration credit posted Sep 8.

- ChatGPT: Sep 26 bill was $60 (2 seats) - done.
- LinkedIn Sales Navigator: cancelled Aug 21 (access to Sep 2) but still charged $99.99 on Sep 3 - DISPUTE.

- Edgegap: still $600/mo (Sep 10). $420 plan requested, not yet confirmed by Edgegap.
- Zoom: no charges since the Jun 12 downgrade to Basic (last charge May 12) - account close is just housekeeping.
- AppMagic (added 9/26): cancelled Sep 27, last charge Sep 14 - $0.

Not on the board yet, but confirmed by the vendors:
- WeWork: ends Sep 30, Sep 1 was the last charge.
- SavvyCal: closed Sep 4 but still charged $16 on Sep 11 - DISPUTE.
- Buttondown: shut down Sep 15 but still charged $20 on Sep 21 - DISPUTE.
- Midjourney: cancelled Jul 3. Aug 2 charge was refunded Aug 25, but charged $60 again on Sep 2 - DISPUTE.

Disputed total: $195.99 (all on card 0417). Card subscription run-rate going into Q4: $3,071.80/mo. Details are on the Q4 run-rate tab of the workbook in Q3 2025 investor reporting: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1VrzayDt_GL6eAHwSyk4qi4qL5JzucULOh7PpzpRscgo/edit

input.subject: Re: Card spend breakdown for Q3 Standard Metrics
input.body:
Leonard,

Done. Adding Robert for the investor update, as you asked. The workbook is in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder: "Q3 2025 Standard Metrics - card spend breakdown (Jan-Sep 2025)"
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1VrzayDt_GL6eAHwSyk4qi4qL5JzucULOh7PpzpRscgo/edit
It has four tabs: By vendor, Category by month, Ledger tie-out, Q4 run-rate. I followed your card close notes: statement cycles by posted date, refunds counted in the cycle they post in, FX fees counted with their charge, and bank-rule vendors and card payments excluded.

TIE-OUT
Every month ties to the Unreconciled operating expenses line in FINANCE_LEDGER to the cent: $97,968.21 for Jan-Sep. Two adjustments:
- June has no ledger line. The June cycle ($12,222.02) plus the July cycle ($12,132.35) make up the July line of $24,354.37.
- August includes a $1,000.00 UNITY ADS charge (Aug 20). I show it as a reclass to marketing UA, not as opex.
That leaves $96,968.21 of non-payroll opex for Jan-Sep.

TOTALS BY GRIFFIN CATEGORY (Q3 = Jul-Sep cycles / Jan-Sep)
- Software & subscriptions: $3,177.52 / $8,361.12
- Hosting & infrastructure: $14,455.70 / $27,305.36
- Research & user testing: $1,075.66 / $2,086.46
- Marketing (non-UA): $1,020.00 / $3,019.00
- Travel & events: $13,032.74 / $23,043.63
- Hardware & equipment: $6,295.80 / $19,203.87
- Professional & admin: $1,837.00 / $7,473.00
- Other G&A: $2,766.34 / $6,475.77
- Total: $43,660.76 / $96,968.21
I used Griffin's answers from Sep 30: the GDC pass goes under Marketing (non-UA) and the Unity seats under Hosting & infrastructure. Q3 Hosting includes the $10,200.00 Unity annual prepay from Aug 8, which is why it's high.

MONTHLY RUN-RATE GOING INTO Q4: $3,071.80/mo
Unity seats $850.00 (1/12 of the annual), Edgegap $600.00, Google Cloud $396.84, Sensor Tower $250.00 (Lite), Carta $230.00 (1/12), Deel $147.00, Gusto $142.00, QuickBooks $90.00, Zapier $73.50, ChatGPT $60.00 (2 seats), Canva $45.00, DocuSign $45.00, Webflow $29.00, Envato $27.04 (1/12), Cogency $25.00 (1/12), 1Password $23.97 (3 seats from Oct), Murf $22.00, Apple Developer $8.25 (1/12), Namecheap $7.20 (1/12).
These are at $0 as confirmed cancellations: WeWork, Notion, AppMagic, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Midjourney, SavvyCal, Buttondown, Zoom, Loom, Supernormal, Backtrace.
Edgegap stays at $600 until Edgegap confirms the $420 plan.

DISPUTED CHARGES: $195.99, all on card 0417, none refunded in the feed through Sep 28
- Midjourney, Sep 2, $60.00. Cancelled Jul 3 (MJ-77k2). The Aug 2 charge was refunded Aug 25, but they billed again on Sep 2.
- LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Sep 3, $99.99. Cancelled Aug 21, with access ending Sep 2.
- SavvyCal, Sep 11, $16.00. Account closed Sep 4.
- Buttondown, Sep 21, $20.00. Newsletter shut down Sep 15.

I put the findings in a comment on your "Q4 cost cuts - card subscriptions" card and left the checklist alone. Arthur's still-charged items (Unity, Edgegap, Google Cloud, 1Password: $1,870.81/mo) are on ENG-2370. None of Arthur's charges are disputed.

Happy to walk through it at Friday's review.

Fred

I've handled everything Leonard asked for in his email, as you. The workbook is in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder, and the reply is sent on his thread. Every month ties to the "Unreconciled operating expenses" ledger line to the cent: $97,968.21 for January–September.

**Ledger tie-out:** I built this from all 496 daily sheets for both cards, including the late refund and credit tabs.
- There's no June line in the ledger. June's spend ($12,222.02) plus July's ($12,132.35) make up the July line of $24,354.37.
- August's line includes a $1,000.00 Unity Ads charge. That's paid user acquisition, so I took it out of the categories and show it as a reclass.
- That leaves $96,968.21 of card opex for January–September.

**Totals by Griffin's categories**

| Category | Q3 (Jul–Sep) | Jan–Sep |
|---|---|---|
| Software & subscriptions | $3,177.52 | $8,361.12 |
| Hosting & infrastructure | $14,455.70 | $27,305.36 |
| Research & user testing | $1,075.66 | $2,086.46 |
| Marketing (non-UA) | $1,020.00 | $3,019.00 |
| Travel & events | $13,032.74 | $23,043.63 |
| Hardware & equipment | $6,295.80 | $19,203.87 |
| Professional & admin | $1,837.00 | $7,473.00 |
| Other G&A | $2,766.34 | $6,475.77 |
| **Total** | **$43,660.76** | **$96,968.21** |

- Griffin's August note left two items open. Leonard passed on his answers in Slack on Sep 30, and I used them: the GDC conference pass goes under Marketing (non-UA), and Unity seats go under Hosting & infrastructure.
- Q3 Hosting looks high because it includes the $10,200 Unity annual prepay from Aug 8.

**Recurring going into Q4: $3,071.80/month.** The biggest pieces are Unity at $850 (1/12 of the annual prepay), Edgegap at $600 and Google Cloud at $396.84. Edgegap stays at $600 because Arthur asked for the cheaper $420 plan but Edgegap hasn't confirmed it. Eleven subscriptions are at $0 because the vendor confirmed the cancellation, including WeWork (ends Sep 30), Notion and AppMagic.

**Cancelled but still charged: $195.99, all on Leonard's card.** None of these had been refunded as of the Sep 28 feed.
- Midjourney, Sep 2, $60.00. Cancelled Jul 3; they refunded the August charge, then billed again.
- LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Sep 3, $99.99. This one is yours: LinkedIn's Aug 21 email to you said you wouldn't be charged again.
- SavvyCal, Sep 11, $16.00.
- Buttondown, Sep 21, $20.00.

**Other updates**
- **Reply recipients:** Leonard said in a Slack DM on Sep 30 to add Robert for the investor update and keep Arthur on, so the reply went to Leonard with Arthur and Robert copied.
- **Workbook sharing:** I shared it with Leonard (edit) and with Arthur and Robert (view only).
- **Trello:** I commented on Leonard's cut-list card with where each item stands and the four disputed charges, and left his checklist alone.
- **Linear:** On Arthur's seat cleanup ticket (ENG-2370), I listed his four subscriptions still being charged: Unity, Edgegap, Google Cloud and 1Password, $1,870.81/month in total. None of his charges are disputed.

Two judgment calls you may want to check:
- **1Password:** I used 3 seats ($23.97/month). Arthur said 4 on the cut list, but Leonard's later note on the 1Password card says 3, confirmed in the admin console.
- **Fiverr ($1,020):** I put it under Marketing (non-UA). Your receipts show it was a store trailer and screenshots.

Leonard's card-spend review is Friday at 10am PT if he wants to go through it.

Files are in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder:
- Q3 2025 Standard Metrics - card spend breakdown (Jan-Sep 2025)
